mainTopic: Giving up honor (רב, נשיא, מלך) and the מצוה of standing for a זקן
overview: This amud asks whether a person who is owed honor can give it up. רבא decides that a רב can, because Torah that a person learns becomes 'his Torah'. Two stories show that even so, people must still show the רב some respect (הידור). רב אשי first says a נשיא cannot give up his honor. The story of רבן גמליאל serving drinks at his son's wedding, defended by רבי יהושע and רבי צדוק, disproves that. So the גמרא restates רב אשי's teaching: a מלך can never give up his honor. Next, a ברייתא explains the מצוה of standing for a זקן: who counts as a זקן, when and where one stands, and that the זקן himself should not trouble people. The גמרא then shows that the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי הגלילי argue about a young חכם. It begins to explain each side's reading of the פסוק, and the argument continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבא: A teacher's Torah is not his own
steps.stepSummary: רבא finishes pushing back on the proof that a רב can waive his honor. The Torah is not the רב's personal property, so he cannot give up its honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, with a human teacher, is the Torah really his?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is completing his rejection of the earlier proof. He says a human רב is different from הקב״ה, because the Torah does not belong to the רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, רבא said הקב״ה can give up His honor because the world and the Torah are His. Here he points out that a human teacher does not own the Torah. So a רב has no right to give up honor that really belongs to the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: here (in our case, a human רב)
giving up something owed to you

phrases.english: Here, is the Torah his?!
phrases.notes: This finishes רבא's thought from just before: there, הקב״ה owns the world and the Torah, so He can give up His honor.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא תּוֹרָה דִּילֵיהּ הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's rejection (from before this section) of רב יוסף's proof that a רב may waive his honor.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects comparing a human רב to הקב״ה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: הקב״ה owns the Torah; a human teacher does not, so he cannot waive its honor.

steps.title: רבא changes his mind: the Torah becomes his
steps.stepSummary: רבא reverses himself. Once a person learns Torah, it is called 'his Torah,' so a רב can give up his honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא then said: Yes, it is his Torah, as it is written: 'And in his Torah he meditates day and night.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא takes back what he just said. Using a פסוק, he now holds that a רב who learns Torah owns it in a real sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק first calls it 'the Torah of ה',' then calls it 'his Torah.' This shows that learning makes the Torah belong to the learner. Since it is his, a רב can waive the honor owed to him because of it.

keyTerms.meaning: he then said (he changed his mind)

steps.whatToRemember: Final view of רבא: a רב who waives his honor, his honor is waived (הרב שמחל על כבודו כבודו מחול), because his Torah truly belongs to him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rest of the section. If a רב can waive his honor, why did רבא himself get upset when people didn't stand for him?

phrases.english: Rava then said:
Yes, the Torah is his,
as it is written:
"And in his Torah he meditates day and night."
phrases.notes: תהלים 1:2. Earlier in the same פסוק it says 'the Torah of ה''. Once he learns it, it's called 'his Torah.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא takes back his rejection from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah that a person learns becomes his, so a רב may waive his honor.

steps.title: רבא got upset when rabbis did not stand for him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that a רב can waive his honor. At his son's wedding רבא served drinks himself, but got angry at two rabbis who did not stand for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רבא was serving drinks at his son's wedding. He lifted a cup for רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, and they stood up for him. For רב מרי and רב פנחס בריה דרב חסדא they did not stand. He got upset and said: Are these rabbis real rabbis, and those rabbis not rabbis?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question against רבא's ruling, using a story about רבא himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By serving drinks, רבא was clearly giving up his honor. If waiving honor really works, the rabbis who stayed seated did nothing wrong. Yet רבא was upset, which suggests his honor was still owed to him.

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But Rava was serving drinks
at his son's wedding feast,
and he lifted a cup

phrases.aramaic: לְרַב פָּפָּא וּלְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
phrases.english: for Rav Pappa and for Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua,
and they stood up before him.

phrases.aramaic: לְרַב מָרִי וּלְרַב פִּנְחָס בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא,
phrases.english: For Rav Mari and for Rav Pinchas son of Rav Chisda,
and they did not stand up before him.
He became upset and said:
Are these rabbis real rabbis,
and those rabbis not rabbis?
phrases.notes: He means: you two act like great Sages who don't need to stand, while the ones who stood aren't?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי וְהָא רָבָא מַשְׁקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's conclusion in step 2 using רבא's own behavior.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a רב who waives his honor, his honor is waived.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא waived his honor by serving drinks, yet still expected people to stand. So his honor was not really waived.

steps.title: A second story: רב פפא also got upset
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a second story. רב פפא served drinks at his son's wedding and got upset when רבי יצחק בריה דרב יהודה did not stand.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, רב פפא was serving drinks at the wedding of his son אבא מר. He lifted a cup for רבי יצחק בריה דרב יהודה, who did not stand up for him, and רב פפא became upset!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes its challenge stronger by bringing another story just like the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story makes the same point again. A רב who was clearly giving up his honor still expected respect, which seems to show the honor was not truly given up.

phrases.english: And furthermore,
Rav Pappa was serving drinks
at the wedding feast of Abba Mar, his son,
and he lifted a cup
for Rabbi Yitzchak son of Rav Yehuda,
and he did not stand up before him, and Rav Pappa became upset!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ רַב פָּפָּא הֲוָה מַשְׁקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second story to strengthen the challenge from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a רב can waive his honor.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another רב who waived his honor still got upset when he was not given respect.

steps.title: Even so, some respect is still needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: a רב can waive his full honor, but people still have to show him some respect (הידור).
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, they need to show him some respect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers both stories. Waiving honor works, but not completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A רב can give up the full honor he is owed, like people standing all the way up. But a smaller sign of respect is still required. The rabbis in the stories showed none at all, which is why רבא and רב פפא were upset.
steps.whatToRemember: A רב may waive his honor, but a basic level of respect (הידור) must still be shown to him.

phrases.english: Even so,
they need to show him some respect.
phrases.notes: הידור here is a smaller show of respect, less than the full honor the רב gave up.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ הָכִי הִידּוּר מֶיעְבַּד לֵיהּ בָּעוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenges of steps 3 and 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits how far the waiver goes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Waiving honor means no respect at all is needed, so the stories contradict the rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The waiver removes the full honor, but a basic sign of respect is still required.

steps.title: רב אשי: a נשיא cannot waive his honor
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי teaches that even if a רב can waive his honor, a נשיא cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Even according to the one who says that a רב who waives his honor, his honor is waived, a נשיא who waives his honor, his honor is not waived.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds a new rule about the נשיא, the head of the Jewish people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי accepts that a רב may give up his honor. But the honor of a נשיא is different. It is not just his own personal honor, so he cannot give it up.

keyTerms.meaning: according to the one who says
the head of the Jewish people / head of the סנהדרין

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a separate rule for a נשיא, and the next step challenges it right away.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Even according to the one who says:
a rav who waives his honor,
his honor is waived,
a Nasi who waives his honor,
his honor is not waived.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי אֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the rule about a רב and adds a stricter rule for a נשיא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נשיא cannot waive his honor, even according to the view that a רב can.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל served drinks at his son's wedding
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אשי with a story. רבן גמליאל, the נשיא, stood and served drinks to Sages at his son's wedding. רבי יהושע accepted the cup, and רבי אליעזר protested.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: There was a story with רבי אליעזר, רבי יהושע and רבי צדוק, who were reclining at the wedding feast of רבן גמליאל's son. רבן גמליאל was standing and serving them drinks. He gave the cup to רבי אליעזר, who did not take it. He gave it to רבי יהושע, who accepted it. רבי אליעזר said to him: What is this, יהושע? We are sitting, and the great רבן גמליאל is standing and serving us drinks?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a challenge against רב אשי using a story from the תנאים. The next two steps finish the story with the answers of רבי יהושע and רבי צדוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל was the נשיא, and he chose to serve the Sages. This looks like a נשיא giving up his honor. רבי יהושע accepted the cup, which suggests that a נשיא can waive his honor, against רב אשי.

keyTerms.meaning: they raised an objection (from a ברייתא)
a title of honor: the great, the esteemed

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not finished yet. רבי אליעזר's protest is only the start. The real challenge to רב אשי is that רבי יהושע accepted the cup. His defense of that comes in step 8, and רבי צדוק adds to it in step 9.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וְרַבִּי צָדוֹק
phrases.english: There was a story with Rabbi Eliezer, Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Tzadok
who were reclining

phrases.aramaic: בְּבֵית הַמִּשְׁתֶּה בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: at the wedding feast of Rabban Gamliel's son,
and Rabban Gamliel was standing
and serving them drinks.
He gave the cup to Rabbi Eliezer
and he did not take it;
he gave it to Rabbi Yehoshua
and he accepted it.
Rabbi Eliezer said to him:
What is this, Yehoshua?
We are sitting
and the great Rabban Gamliel is standing
and serving us drinks?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי מַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וְרַבִּי צָדוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's rule from step 6 with a ברייתא story.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's rule that a נשיא cannot waive his honor.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבן גמליאל, the נשיא, served the Sages and רבי יהושע accepted the cup. That suggests a נשיא's waiver of honor does work.

steps.title: רבי יהושע's proof from אברהם
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע answers רבי אליעזר. אברהם was even greater than רבן גמליאל, and he still stood and served guests he thought were ordinary travelers.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We know of someone greater than רבן גמליאל who served others. אברהם was greater, and he served. אברהם was the greatest man of his generation, and the תורה says about him, "And he stood over them." You might say he served them only because they looked like angels. No, they looked to him like ordinary Arab travelers. So why shouldn't the great רבן גמליאל stand and serve us drinks?
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the story, רבי יהושע defends taking the cup from רבן גמליאל. He brings a proof from אברהם אבינו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר objected to letting the נשיא serve them. רבי יהושע shows that a far greater man, אברהם, served guests himself. He also blocks a possible rebuttal: אברהם did not think his guests were angels, so he was serving ordinary people.

keyTerms.meaning: the greatest person of the generation
the esteemed one, a title of honor

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מָצִינוּ גָּדוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ שֶׁשִּׁמֵּשׁ,
phrases.english: He said to him: We have found someone greater than him who served,
phrases.notes: רבי יהושע is speaking to רבי אליעזר. "Him" means רבן גמליאל.

phrases.english: Avraham was greater than him, and he served.
Avraham was the greatest of his generation,
and it is written about him: "And he stood over them."

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁמָּא תֹּאמְרוּ: כְּמַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת נִדְמוּ לוֹ –
phrases.english: And perhaps you will say: they looked to him like ministering angels.
No, they looked to him only like Arabs.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָנוּ, לֹא יְהֵא רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בְּרִיבִּי
phrases.english: And as for us, should the esteemed Rabban Gamliel not
stand and serve us drinks?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מָצִינוּ גָּדוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ שֶׁשִּׁמֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from step 7. It is רבי יהושע's reply to רבי אליעזר's protest.
steps.raayaObject: That it is proper for a great person like the נשיא to serve others
steps.raayaSupportSource: אברהם standing over his guests (בראשית 18:8), whom he thought were ordinary Arabs

steps.title: רבי צדוק's proof from ה׳ Himself
steps.stepSummary: רבי צדוק brings a stronger proof. הקדוש ברוך הוא provides food and rain for every creature, so רבן גמליאל can certainly serve the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי צדוק said to them: How long will you ignore the honor of ה׳ and talk only about the honor of people? הקדוש ברוך הוא makes the winds blow, brings up the clouds, sends rain, makes the ground grow food, and sets a table for every single creature. So why shouldn't the great רבן גמליאל stand and serve us drinks?
steps.whatsHappening: A third חכם, רבי צדוק, joins in. He says there is an even better proof than אברהם‎: ה׳ Himself serves His creatures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי צדוק says they should learn from how ה׳ acts, not only from people. If ה׳ takes care of everyone's needs, serving others is no insult to a great person. This story ends the challenge from step 7: a נשיא clearly can give up his honor.

keyTerms.meaning: the honor of ה׳‎ (מקום is a name for ה׳)

steps.whyThisMatters: This story is why the גמרא has to take back the earlier version of רב אשי's teaching, since a נשיא did give up his honor.

phrases.english: Rabbi Tzadok said to them:

phrases.aramaic: עַד מָתַי אַתֶּם מַנִּיחִים כְּבוֹדוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם
phrases.english: How long will you leave aside the honor of the Omnipresent
and busy yourselves with the honor of people?
The Holy One, Blessed be He, makes the winds blow,
and raises clouds, and brings down rain,
phrases.notes: Here נשיאים means clouds, not leaders.

phrases.english: and makes the ground sprout,

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹרֵךְ שׁוּלְחָן לִפְנֵי כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד,
phrases.english: and sets a table before each and every one.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָנוּ לֹא יְהֵא רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בְּרִיבִּי
phrases.english: And as for us, should the esteemed Rabban Gamliel not
stand and serve us drinks?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם רַבִּי צָדוֹק: עַד מָתַי אַתֶּם מַנִּיחִים כְּבוֹדוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens רבי יהושע's proof from אברהם with a proof from ה׳ Himself.
steps.raayaObject: That a great person, even the נשיא, may serve others
steps.raayaSupportSource: הקדוש ברוך הוא provides wind, rain, crops and food for every creature

steps.title: רב אשי's teaching restated: a king cannot give up his honor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that a נשיא can give up his honor and restates רב אשי's teaching. Even according to the view that a נשיא can give it up, a מלך cannot, because the תורה says the king's awe must be upon you.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if רב אשי said something, this is what he said: Even according to the one who holds that a נשיא who gives up his honor has truly given it up, a king who gives up his honor has not. The פסוק says, "You shall surely set a king over you," which teaches that the fear of him must be upon you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits the story shows a נשיא can give up his honor. So it changes the version of רב אשי's teaching to talk about a מלך instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, רב אשי was quoted as saying a נשיא cannot give up his honor, and the story of רבן גמליאל disproved that. Now he is quoted as saying a מלך cannot give up his honor. A king is different because the תורה commands that people must stand in awe of him, so this is not his personal right to give away.

keyTerms.meaning: if it was said, this is how it was said (the גמרא restates a teaching)

steps.whatToRemember: The order is: a רב can give up his honor (but people still show him הידור). A נשיא can give up his honor, as the story of רבן גמליאל shows. A מלך can never give up his honor, because the תורה requires that people be in awe of him.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is rejecting רב אשי. It keeps his teaching but corrects what he said: a מלך, not a נשיא.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said:
Rav Ashi said:
Even according to the one who says:

phrases.aramaic: נָשִׂיא שֶׁמָּחַל עַל כְּבוֹדוֹ – כְּבוֹדוֹ מָחוּל,
phrases.english: a Nasi who gives up his honor, his honor is given up,

phrases.aramaic: מֶלֶךְ שֶׁמָּחַל עַל כְּבוֹדוֹ – אֵין כְּבוֹדוֹ מָחוּל,
phrases.english: a king who gives up his honor, his honor is not given up,
as it is said: "You shall surely set a king over you,"
meaning that the fear of him should be upon you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אִיתְּמַר הָכִי אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the רבן גמליאל story by restating רב אשי's teaching.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Restating the teaching (changing what רב אשי actually said)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אשי said a נשיא cannot give up his honor.
steps.terutzMaskana: A נשיא can give up his honor, but a מלך cannot, because of ״שום תשים עליך מלך״.

steps.title: Standing for an elder means standing for a Torah scholar
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the פסוק ״מפני שיבה תקום״. The תנא קמא says the מצוה is not for every old, unlearned man. A זקן means a חכם, as the elders appointed in the desert were.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: "Before a gray head you shall rise." Could this mean even before an old man who is unlearned? The פסוק says "זקן," and a זקן means only a wise person, as it says: "Gather for Me seventy men from the elders of Israel."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא about the מצוה to stand up for a זקן. It asks who counts as a זקן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading only ״מפני שיבה תקום״, we might think we must stand for every old man. The ברייתא uses the word ״זקן״ in the same פסוק to say that a זקן is a חכם. It proves this from the seventy זקנים appointed in the desert, who were leaders and wise men.

keyTerms.meaning: before a gray head you shall rise
a זקן means only a wise person

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"Before a gray head you shall rise."
Could it be even before an unlearned old man?
The verse says: "elder,"
and an elder is nothing other than a wise person,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אֶסְפָה לִּי שִׁבְעִים אִישׁ מִזִּקְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל״.
phrases.english: as it is said: "Gather for Me seventy men of the elders of Israel."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״מִפְּנֵי שֵׂיבָה תָּקוּם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about the מצוה of standing for a זקן, after the discussion of giving up honor.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מצוה of standing up applies to a זקן who is a חכם, not to an unlearned old man.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי: a זקן is someone who has gained wisdom
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי gives his own reading. A זקן is someone who has acquired wisdom, and he proves this from a פסוק where wisdom says ״ה׳ קנני״.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי הגלילי says: A זקן is only someone who has acquired wisdom, as it says: "ה׳ acquired me at the beginning of His way."
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the ברייתא explains the word זקן in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי reads the word זקן as "זה קנה", meaning "this one acquired." He shows that "acquiring" goes with wisdom from a פסוק in משלי where wisdom says ה׳ "acquired" it. So a זקן is defined by the wisdom he has gained.
steps.whatToRemember: The first two opinions in the ברייתא both tie the מצוה of standing up to wisdom. The תנא קמא learns it from the זקנים in the desert, and רבי יוסי הגלילי reads זקן as "זה קנה", one who acquired wisdom. Step 20 shows the practical difference between them: a young חכם. Later in the ברייתא, איסי בן יהודה (step 18) includes every old person.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין זָקֵן אֶלָּא מִי שֶׁקָּנָה חׇכְמָה,
phrases.english: an elder is nothing other than one who has acquired wisdom,
phrases.notes: He reads זקן as "זה קנה", meaning "this one acquired."

phrases.english: as it is said: "ה׳ acquired me at the beginning of His way."
phrases.notes: משלי 8:22. In this פסוק, wisdom is the one speaking.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר: אֵין זָקֵן אֶלָּא מִי שֶׁקָּנָה חׇכְמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second opinion in the same ברייתא, giving another way to read the word זקן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זקן is one who has acquired wisdom (זה קנה), learned from ״ה׳ קנני ראשית דרכו״.

steps.title: No standing from far away
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא teaches that one does not have to stand for a זקן who is still far away, because the standing must be a visible act of honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think you must stand for him even from far away. So the פסוק says "stand and honor": I only required standing in a place where it shows honor.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues explaining the פסוק ״תקום והדרת״. It rules out standing for a זקן who is still far off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links standing (קימה) with honoring (הידור). So standing only counts when it is clearly seen as honor. When the זקן is far away, nobody can tell that you are standing for him.

keyTerms.meaning: "One might think". It introduces a mistaken idea that the פסוק will rule out.
"The verse teaches". It introduces the proof from the פסוק.

phrases.english: One might think he must stand before him even from a distance?
The verse says: "You shall stand and you shall honor"
I did not say standing
except in a place where there is honor.
phrases.notes: Standing up for someone who is still far off doesn't look like you're honoring him.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל יַעֲמוֹד מִפָּנָיו מִמָּקוֹם רָחוֹק? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא on ״מפני שיבה תקום״, now setting the limits of the מצוה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One stands for a זקן only when he is close enough that the standing is a clear act of honor.

steps.title: Honor does not cost money
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from the pairing of standing and honoring that the required honor costs no money.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think you must honor him with money. So the פסוק says "stand and honor": just as standing costs no money, so too the honor is one that costs no money.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks whether honoring a זקן means spending money on him. It answers no.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא compares honoring to standing, since the פסוק puts them side by side. Standing costs nothing, so the honor required must also cost nothing. Examples are respectful behavior, not gifts.

keyTerms.meaning: Monetary loss. Literally, "a loss of the pocket."
"Just as... so too...". A comparison between two things

phrases.english: One might think he should honor him with money?
The verse says: "You shall stand and you shall honor"

phrases.aramaic: מָה קִימָה שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ חֶסְרוֹן כִּיס,
phrases.english: Just as standing involves no monetary loss,

phrases.aramaic: אַף הִידּוּר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ חֶסְרוֹן כִּיס.
phrases.english: so too, the honor is one that involves no monetary loss.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל יְהַדְּרֶנּוּ בְּמָמוֹן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another limit on the same מצוה, learned from the same words ״תקום והדרת״.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Honoring a זקן does not require spending money.

steps.title: No standing in a lavatory or bathhouse
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that one does not stand for a זקן in a lavatory or bathhouse, because those are not places of honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think you should stand for him in the lavatory or the bathhouse. So the פסוק says "stand and honor": I only required standing in a place where there is honor.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rules out standing for a זקן in a lavatory or a bathhouse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It uses the same line as step 13, "only in a place where there is honor." Here it is about the kind of place, not the distance. Showing respect in such places is not fitting.

keyTerms.meaning: A place where showing honor is fitting

steps.confusionAlert: This uses the exact same words as step 13, but it teaches something new. Step 13 was about distance. This step is about places where honor doesn't belong.

phrases.english: One might think he should stand before him
in the lavatory and in the bathhouse?
The verse says: "You shall stand and you shall honor"
I did not say standing
except in a place where there is honor.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל יַעֲמוֹד מִפָּנָיו מִבֵּית הַכִּסֵּא וּמִבֵּית הַמֶּרְחָץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reuses the derivation from step 13 for a new kind of case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no obligation to stand for a זקן in a lavatory or bathhouse.

steps.title: No pretending you didn't see him
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא forbids shutting one's eyes to avoid standing for a זקן. Since only he and God know the truth, the פסוק adds ״ויראת מאלהיך״.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think he may shut his eyes as if he never saw the זקן. So the פסוק says "stand... and fear": about anything that only the heart knows, the תורה says "and you shall fear your God."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא closes a loophole. A person may not pretend not to see the זקן so that he can avoid standing up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one else can prove whether he really didn't see. That is why the פסוק ends with ״ויראת מאלהיך״. God knows what is in his heart, so the fear of God is what makes him keep the מצוה honestly.

keyTerms.meaning: A matter given over to the heart, which only the person himself knows

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule: whenever the תורה says ״ויראת מאלהיך״, it is about something only the person and God can know.

phrases.english: One might think he may shut his eyes
as if he did not see him?
The verse says: "You shall stand... and you shall fear"
phrases.notes: The dots skip the middle of the same פסוק, ויקרא 19:32.

phrases.english: A matter given over to the heart
phrases.notes: Something no one else can check. Only he knows if he really didn't see.

phrases.english: about it is said: "and you shall fear your God."

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל יַעֲצִים עֵינָיו כְּמִי שֶׁלֹּא רָאָהוּ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting limits on the מצוה, the ברייתא now prevents people from dodging it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not pretend not to see a זקן in order to avoid standing. The fear of God holds him to it.

steps.title: The elder should not burden others
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר reads ״זקן ויראת״ as a command to the זקן himself: he should not go out of his way to make people stand for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: How do we know that a זקן should not trouble people? The פסוק says "an elder, and you shall fear."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר turns the מצוה around and gives a responsibility to the זקן himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the words ״זקן ויראת״ together, as if they say "the זקן should fear God." So the זקן must not deliberately walk in front of people just to make them stand up for him.

keyTerms.meaning: "From where?" Asking for the source of a law
"An elder, and you shall fear". Read here as a message to the זקן

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
From where do we know that an elder should not trouble others?
The verse says: "an elder, and you shall fear."
phrases.notes: He reads these two words together, so the זקן himself must fear God.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: מִנַּיִן לְזָקֵן שֶׁלֹּא יַטְרִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same word ״ויראת״ from step 16, but applies it to the זקן rather than to the one standing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זקן should not go out of his way to make people stand for him.

steps.title: Any old person is included
steps.stepSummary: איסי בן יהודה disagrees with the view in step 11. He holds that ״מפני שיבה תקום״ includes every old person, even one who is not a חכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: איסי בן יהודה says: "Before the gray head you shall stand" means any gray head at all is included.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with איסי בן יהודה, who disagrees about who counts as a זקן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא in step 11 limited the מצוה to a חכם. איסי בן יהודה reads ״שיבה״ simply, as gray hair. So any old person, learned or not, deserves that we stand for him.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who disagrees with the תנא קמא here

steps.whatToRemember: There are two views on ״מפני שיבה תקום״. The תנא קמא says it applies only to a חכם. איסי בן יהודה says it applies to every old person.

phrases.english: Isi ben Yehuda says:
"Before the gray head you shall stand"
even any gray head is included in the meaning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיסִי בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: ״מִפְּנֵי שֵׂיבָה תָּקוּם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the question from steps 11-12 of who is a זקן, and gives a broader answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מצוה of standing applies to every old person, not only a חכם.

steps.title: Is רבי יוסי הגלילי saying anything new?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יוסי הגלילי's view is the same as the תנא קמא's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't רבי יוסי הגלילי saying the same thing as the first תנא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that both opinions in the ברייתא seem to say that a זקן means a wise person. It asks what the difference between them is, and this sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי הגלילי define זקן through wisdom. If they say the same thing, why are they listed as two opinions? The גמרא wants to find the practical difference.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה
A תנא who defines זקן as one who has acquired wisdom

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי הַיְינוּ תַּנָּא קַמָּא?
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili is the same as the first tanna?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי הַיְינוּ תַּנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא's two opinions about who counts as a זקן and asks how they differ.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical difference exists between the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי הגלילי?

steps.title: They argue about a young wise person
steps.stepSummary: The difference between them is a young person who is wise. The תנא קמא says no, and רבי יוסי הגלילי says even he must be honored.
steps.simpleTranslation: They differ about someone young and wise. The first תנא holds that a young wise person does not get this honor. רבי יוסי הגלילי holds that even a young wise person does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by showing a case where the two opinions give different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, the person must be both old and wise. For רבי יוסי הגלילי, only wisdom matters, so age is not needed at all. A young חכם is where this makes a real difference.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא requires old and wise. רבי יוסי הגלילי requires only wise, even if young.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them: one who is young and wise.
phrases.notes: יניק literally means a nursing baby. Here it just means someone young.

phrases.english: The first tanna holds:
one who is young and wise, no;
Rabbi Yosei HaGelili holds:
even one who is young and wise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ יַנִּיק וְחַכִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They argue about a young wise person. The תנא קמא excludes him, and רבי יוסי הגלילי includes him.

steps.title: What is רבי יוסי הגלילי's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי יוסי הגלילי's view that a young wise person is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reasoning of רבי יוסי הגלילי?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know what they argue about, the גמרא asks how רבי יוסי הגלילי learns his view from the פסוק. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants to see which detail in the wording of the פסוק shows that age is not needed.

phrases.english: What is the reasoning of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the view stated in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which textual basis shows that a young wise person is included?

steps.title: The verse separates hoary head from elder
steps.stepSummary: If the תנא קמא were right, the תורה would have joined שיבה and זקן together. Since the פסוק separates them, they are two different people, so a young wise person counts as a זקן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: if you think it is like the first תנא says, then the תורה should have written 'Before a hoary-headed elder you shall stand and honor.' Why did the תורה split them apart? To tell us that this one is not that one, and that one is not this one. Learn from this that even a young wise person is included.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רבי יוסי הגלילי learns his view from how the פסוק is built: שיבה is at the beginning and זקן is at the end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one person had to be both old and wise, the two words would sit together. Splitting them shows that שיבה (an old person) and זקן (a wise person) are separate categories. So a זקן does not need to be old, and even a young חכם must be honored.

keyTerms.meaning: If it enters your mind (if you were to think)
Let the Torah (literally 'the Merciful One') write

steps.confusionAlert: Here רבי יוסי הגלילי reads שיבה and זקן as two different people. He is not saying a wise old man loses his honor. He is saying that wisdom alone is already enough for a זקן.

phrases.english: He would say to you:

phrases.aramaic: אִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ כִּדְקָאָמַר תַּנָּא קַמָּא –
phrases.english: if it enters your mind that it is as the first tanna says,
if so, let the Merciful One write:
"Before a hoary-headed elder you shall stand and you shall honor";
phrases.notes: The real פסוק (ויקרא 19:32) puts זקן at the end. This is how it would read if the two words were joined.

phrases.english: what is different, that the Merciful One separated them?
To say: that this one is not that one,
and that one is not this one.
Learn from it: even one who is young and wise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ אִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ כִּדְקָאָמַר תַּנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 21 with a reading of the פסוק's word order.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק separates שיבה from זקן, which shows they are different people. So a young חכם counts as a זקן.

steps.title: The תנא קמא explains why the words are separated
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא answers that זקן is placed at the end so that it sits right next to ויראת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the first תנא would say the words are separated because the תורה wanted to put 'elder' right next to 'and you shall fear.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the תנא קמא against רבי יוסי הגלילי's proof. It gives a different reason why the פסוק separates the words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The separation does not have to mean two different people. It can be there so that זקן sits next to ויראת, which is the lesson of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר in step 17. This lesson teaches the זקן not to burden people to stand for him. So the proof from the word order is taken away.

keyTerms.meaning: To place next to, to put side by side
And you shall fear (the next word in the פסוק)

phrases.english: And the first tanna?
Because it wants to place "elder" next to "and you shall fear."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנָּא קַמָּא מִשּׁוּם דְּבָעֵי לְמִיסְמַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוסי הגלילי's proof in step 22 on behalf of the תנא קמא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different purpose for the same textual feature
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The separation of שיבה from זקן proves they are two different people.
steps.terutzMaskana: The separation is there to place זקן next to ויראת, as רבי שמעון בן אלעזר taught.

steps.title: What is the תנא קמא's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the תנא קמא holds that the person must be both old and wise.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reasoning of the first תנא?
steps.whatsHappening: After defending the תנא קמא, the גמרא now asks for his positive source. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Defending against a proof is not the same as having a source. The גמרא wants to know what in the פסוק shows that age and wisdom must go together.

phrases.english: And the first tanna, what is his reasoning?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנָּא קַמָּא מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defending the תנא קמא to asking for his own source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the textual basis for requiring someone both old and wise?

steps.title: The תנא קמא begins his own argument from the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא begins to argue that if רבי יוסי הגלילי were right, the תורה would have written the פסוק differently. The rest of the argument comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think it is like רבי יוסי הגלילי says, then the תורה should have written:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts the תנא קמא's answer, using the same 'the תורה should have written it differently' style. The sentence continues on the next amud, so this step only sets up the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא turns רבי יוסי הגלילי's method back against him. He will show that a different wording would have been expected if wisdom alone were enough. The other wording itself has not been quoted yet.

phrases.aramaic: אִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ כִּדְקָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי –
phrases.english: If it enters your mind that it is as Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says,
if so, let the Merciful One write:

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ כִּדְקָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 24 with the same kind of argument רבי יוסי הגלילי used in step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Partial: if רבי יוסי הגלילי were right, the פסוק would have been worded differently. The exact wording comes on the next amud.
